newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Ashok Leyland opens truck plant.
newsitem.headline: India's Ashok Leyland opens truck plant.

text.p: India's Ashok Leyland on Saturday inaugurated a state-of-the-art plant to manufacture heavy commercial vehicles in the southern state of Tamil Nadu, company officals said.
Ashok Leyland is a flagship company of the Hinduja group, one of India's richest non-resident investors.
S.P. Hinduja, chairman of the group told reporters the plant, built some 45 km (28 miles) from Bangalore, cost of 6.3 billion rupees ($176 million).
He said the plant, besides producing trucks for the domestic market, has also potential to cater to European, Asian and African markets.
"India has joined the ranks of world class automotive producers like Japan and Korea," Hinduja said.
Hinduja told Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, who attended the inauguration ceremony, that the government should clear all fast track projects by December 24.
He said the delays in clearing projects were frustrating but his group remained committed to a six billion dollar investment programme in India.
Hinduja also called on Gowda to ban entry of foreign players into the Indian media market in order to protect the country's culture.

Gowda said his government remained committed to economic liberalisaton. He also used the opportunity to promote a meeting with industrialists, financiers and academics in Delhi on December 31 to discuss how to advance liberalisation.
